newsitem.title: USA: Domenici, Kasich differ on U.S. budget talks.
newsitem.headline: Domenici, Kasich differ on U.S. budget talks.

text.p: Senate Budget Committee chairman Pete Domenici said Wednesday he remained optimistic that a budget deal would be reached with the White House soon, but his House counterpart, Rep. John Kasich, was skeptical.

"Essentially, I remain positive. I still think the issues that separate us are very big, very important. But I am willing to say come next week we are apt to be finished and we are apt to get a budget," Domenici said. Kasich said he asked the White House to show where cuts in spending should be made. "I don't know what they are willing to give up," he said.

"Our position is we don't want any new programs. We don't want any new spending," Kasich, an Ohio Republican, said at the conclusion of the day's closed door budget talks with Democrats and White House officials.
But Kasich said his comments should not be interpreted as pessimism on the chances of reaching a budget deal. The next step would be discussions on where each side could give up some of its goals.
Domenici said the week met his goals for progress on the budget. Earlier he said this was the "make it or break it week", which would determine the chances of reaching a balanced budget agreement.

"The Democrats and the White House are beginning to understand what we need and I believe they are doing some good in coming our way on some of them. We are beginning to understand some of their concerns," said Domenici, a New Mexico Republican.
Asked if the talks "made it" even though there was no firm agreement to take to the White House, Domenici replied: "Yes, I think so."
